Read the tablewise tests of independence of a fit

Source: R/tidy-accessors.R
tests.Rd

tests() returns the tablewise tests of independence of a fit, one row per test. They test whether the table as a whole departs from independence: whether the state at one time carries any information about the state lag events later (Bakeman & Quera, 1995). The likelihood-ratio statistic \(G^2\) and the Pearson \(\chi^2\) statistic test this omnibus hypothesis against a chi-square distribution, and are read before individual transitions are interpreted.

The tests are computed by the classical engine; the other built-in engines test cells only, and tests() then returns a table with no rows.

Usage

tests(fit)

# S3 method for class 'lsa'
tests(fit)

# S3 method for class 'lsa_group'
tests(fit)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit from lsa(), or a grouped fit from lsa(..., group = ).

Value

A data.frame with one row per test and the columns test ("lrx2" for the likelihood-ratio test, "x2" for Pearson's test), statistic, df and p. A grouped fit gains a leading group column.

References

Bakeman, R., & Quera, V. (1995). Analyzing interaction: Sequential analysis with SDIS and GSEQ. Cambridge University Press.

See also

transitions() for the cell-wise tests; nodes(); lsa-methods for summary().

Examples

tests(lsa(engagement))
#>   test statistic df             p
#> 1 lrx2  618.3053  4 1.691520e-132
#> 2   x2  629.2022  4 7.406567e-135
